fact: SimoCash, launched in May 2026, carries payments and money transfers over mobile money networks such as Orange Money in Cote d'Ivoire.
The article says SimoCash lets funds move directly from one mobile money operator to another, Orange Money being named as one.
BCEAO data show the electronic money usage rate in Cote d'Ivoire at 84.2% in 2024, up from 61% in 2019.

Africtelegraph reports that Orange Money, MTN Mobile Money and Wave have converted millions of Ivorians to mobile money transactions, which merchants, metered taxis and ride-hailing platforms have largely adopted.
system: Orange Money, MTN Mobile Money, Wave

fact: Mobile money points of sale in Cote d'Ivoire have charged an unofficial 100 FCFA agency fee on each deposit or withdrawal since November 2025, on top of the operator tariff of generally 1% on withdrawals, per KOACI.

Electronic money institutions Orange, Wave, MTN and Moov run mobile money in Cote d'Ivoire through small agents at neighbourhood kiosks who verify clients' ID at withdrawal and are told by the operators to keep a copy, per Ivoirexpress.
Fraternite Matin, citing GSMA, says the UEMOA had over 130 million mobile money accounts in 2024, nearly 40% active, and telecoms handle over 80% of electronic transactions.

Fraternite Matin reports PI-SPI, launched by the BCEAO on 30 September 2025, lets users transfer instantly between bank accounts, mobile money wallets and microfinance accounts, with 80 institutions connected.
Orange Money, MTN Mobile Money and Moov Money are the existing electronic-money institutions in Cote d'Ivoire, joined by Djogana Pay's Peya Pay licensed by the BCEAO.
system: Orange Money; MTN Mobile Money; Moov Money

fact: Clotchor Secongo says he built the distribution and e-money management network of TresorPay, the Treasury's electronic payment platform, which now employs over 4,500 distributors across the country.

APAnews reports the fintech PUSH in Cote d'Ivoire has over 700,000 individual accounts and over 20 million transactions worth more than CFAF 600 billion, with an interoperability and merchant-payment agreement signed with Orange Money.
A CGAP/OQSF CI/APIF survey of 10-29 August 2024 reports mobile money users in Côte d'Ivoire using deposit and withdrawal services (97%), bill payment (44%) and merchant payment (22%).
Digital Mag says the app subscription of FCFA 1,000 a year is paid by mobile money (Orange Money, Wave, Moov Money).
Minister Adama Coulibaly says electronic money is distributed through Tresor Money, with FCFA 45 billion exchanged among 545,000 clients in 2024.
Colonel Aly Samassi of Anssi says people in Côte d'Ivoire pay for energy, both electricity and vehicle fuel, by mobile money.
